summary: Martina Palladino is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned degrees at the University of Bologna and SOAS University of London. She has held posts as Adjunct Professor at Bologna and Postdoc Researcher at Ghent University (2023).
Martine Kropman is an Indologist who has conducted doctoral research at the University of Groningen and Leiden University, studying under doctoral supervisor Peter C. Bisschop (attested 2026).

Martino Dibeltulo specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan under the doctoral supervision of Donald S. Lopez Jr. and also studied under mentor Ester Bianchi.

Marvin Eisenberg (1922–2016) was a historian and archaeologist who studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1939–1943) and Princeton University (~1946–1954). He held a faculty post at the University of Michigan from circa 1949 to 1988.
Mary Anne Cartelli specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Columbia University under the doctoral supervision of Philip Boas Yampolsky (attested 1999).

Mary Belle Harris (1874–1957) was an Indologist who studied at Keystone Academy, Bucknell University, Johns Hopkins University, and the University of Chicago (PhD in Sanskrit, ~1897–1900). She taught at the American School of Classical Studies in Rome (1912–1914).

Mary Boyce (1920–2006) specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and religion. Educated at Cambridge and SOAS under Vladimir Minorsky, Harold Walter Bailey, and Walter Bruno Henning, she served at SOAS as Lecturer, Reader, and Professor (1963–1982).

Mary Cecilia Foley (1859–1925) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She graduated with a B.Sc. from University College London by 1891 and served as Chief Lady Invigilator at the University of London from 1901 to 1925.

Mary Clabaugh Wright (1917–1970) was a Sinologist and historian educated at Vassar College and Radcliffe College (MA, PhD). She served as curator of Stanford's China collection (1947) and later as associate professor and full professor at Yale University (1959, 1964).

Mary Evelyn Tucker is a scholar of religious studies, Sinology, and Japanology. Educated at Duke, Columbia, and UCLA, she has held posts as Professor of Religion at Bucknell University (~1989–2005) and Professor at Yale University (~2006).

Mary Haas (1910–1996) was a linguist who studied at Earlham College, the University of Chicago, and Yale University, working under Edward Sapir (~1931–1935). She held a long-term academic appointment at the University of California, Berkeley (~1941–1977).
Mary Jaksch is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at the University of Sunderland under Peter Harvey (attested 2007) and with traditional teacher Ross Bolleter.

Mary Shepherd Slusser (1918–2017) was a historian and Indologist educated at Michigan, Columbia, NYU, and Harvard. She worked for the U.S. Department of State (1951–1958) and held posts at the National Museum of African Art and National Museum of Asian Art.
Marybeth White works in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at York University and later pursued doctoral studies at Wilfrid Laurier University (attested 2006).

Maryla Falk (1906–1980) was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied under Stanisław Schayer (~1932–1938). She held a post at the University of Warsaw (~1935–1939) and was a Fellow of the Royal Asiatic Society (1974).

Marylin Martin Rhie is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. Mentored by Harrie Vanderstappen and Pramod Chandra, she served as a professor at Smith College (attested 1986).

Marzenna Jakubczak is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who earned her PhD at Jagiellonian University and habilitation at Maria Curie-Skłodowska University. She has held posts at the Pedagogical University of Krakow and Jagiellonian University (Associate Professor, 2024).

Masaaki Chikusa (1930–2015) was a scholar of Sinology, history, and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate from Kyoto University. He served in assistant and associate posts at Kyoto University before becoming a professor at Otani University (~1993–2001).

Masaaki Hattori is an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and philosopher educated at Kyoto University and the University of Calcutta under teachers including Gadjin Nagao and Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He taught at Kyoto University (1961–1988) and Hanazono University (~1990–1996).

Masaaki Nitta is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed doctoral coursework at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Fukui Prefectural College (attested 1983–1991) and Fukui Prefectural University (attested 1988).
